subject: community-medicine
title: Tetanus Prevention: Neonatal Elimination, Vaccines and Wound Care

steps.title: Pathogenesis and tetanospasmin exotoxin
steps.tx: The strictly anaerobic spore-forming bacillus Clostridium tetani produces **generalised tetanus**, entering through lacerations, puncture wounds, animal bites or dirty surgical procedures. When necrotic tissue provides an anaerobic redox potential, multiplying bacilli release the lethal exotoxin tetanospasmin, which travels intra-axonally into spinal inhibitory interneurons, permanently cleaving synaptobrevin to block GABA and glycine release and producing uninhibited, agonizing muscular spasms.
steps.say: Tetanus spores multiply in dirty puncture wounds devoid of oxygen. The toxin travels along nerves to block inhibitory neurotransmitters, locking muscles into agonizing, unrelenting spasms.

steps.title: Neonatal tetanus: umbilical cord entry
steps.tx: Historically responsible for immense infant mortality, **neonatal tetanus** results from unhygienic umbilical cord dressing, applying cow dung, ash or contaminated earth to the freshly severed stump, or severing the cord with unsterile blades. Presenting typically around the seventh day of life, previously healthy vigorous infants stop breastfeeding, develop severe trismus preventing suckling, clench their fists, and progress to generalized spasms with high fever.
steps.say: Neonatal tetanus strikes babies when unsterile blades or dirty cow dung dressings contaminate the umbilical stump. By the seventh day, the infant stops feeding and develops body spasms.

steps.title: Validation of maternal and neonatal tetanus elimination
steps.tx: India achieved official international validation for **maternal and neonatal tetanus elimination** in 2015, maintaining an annual neonatal tetanus incidence of less than one case per one thousand live births in every single district. This public health triumph was driven by the National Health Mission through institutional delivery expansion under Janani Suraksha Yojana, promoting the five clean practices at birth, and ensuring universal antenatal tetanus immunization.
steps.say: India eliminated maternal and neonatal tetanus by achieving less than one case per thousand live births across all districts, powered by hospital births and antenatal immunization.

Maternal IgG crosses placenta to shield infant

steps.title: Transition from tetanus toxoid to Td vaccine
steps.tx: The national immunisation programme transitioned from monovalent tetanus toxoid to **tetanus and diphtheria toxoid**, delivering zero point five millilitres intramuscularly. This policy update addresses the re-emergence of adult diphtheria by co-administering reduced-dose diphtheria toxoid alongside tetanus toxoid, sustaining high population antibody titres against both pathogens during school booster sessions at ten years and sixteen years as well as throughout pregnancy.
steps.say: The national program replaced pure tetanus toxoid with combined tetanus and diphtheria vaccine. This protects mothers and adolescents against both tetanus and adult diphtheria outbreaks.

right.title: Modern Td vaccine
points: Standard in pregnancy, schools and wound care

steps.title: Antenatal immunization protocol for pregnant women
steps.tx: Every pregnant woman receives structured **antenatal Td prophylaxis** to induce maternal IgG antibodies that transfer across the placenta to confer passive immunity to the newborn. If unimmunised previously, she receives two doses of Td four weeks apart, with the first dose given early in pregnancy; if she received two doses in a pregnancy within the preceding three years, a single booster dose suffices.
steps.say: Pregnant mothers receive two doses of Td four weeks apart. Maternal antibodies travel across the placenta, shielding the newborn baby from umbilical tetanus during the first months of life.

rows: Two doses of Td (0.5 ml IM)
Td-1 early in pregnancy; Td-2 after 4 weeks
Single booster dose of Td (0.5 ml IM)
Second dose at least 2 weeks before delivery

steps.title: Tetanus immunoglobulin for passive immunization
steps.tx: In unimmunised patients suffering severe contaminated wounds, immediate passive immunity is provided by **human tetanus immunoglobulin**, administered intramuscularly at a dose of two hundred and fifty international units (or five hundred units for severe, contaminated wounds). Because injected antibodies provide instant toxin neutralization before active vaccine immunity can develop, it is administered at a separate anatomical site using a separate syringe from the Td vaccine.
steps.say: Human tetanus immunoglobulin provides instant antibodies to neutralize toxin in dirty wounds before the patient can make their own. Always inject it at a separate site from the vaccine.

left.title: Human tetanus immunoglobulin (HTIG)
points: No serum sickness; half-life 3 to 4 weeks

right.title: Active Td vaccine

steps.title: Evidence-based post-exposure wound management
steps.tx: Emergency triage follows standardized **wound prophylaxis guidelines**, categorising wounds into clean minor versus dirty contaminated wounds, based on soil contamination, animal bites, devitalised tissue or delays exceeding six hours. Clean minor wounds require only a Td booster if more than ten years have elapsed since the last dose; contaminated dirty wounds receive a Td booster if more than five years elapsed, plus HTIG if unimmunised.
steps.say: Clean minor wounds need a tetanus booster only if ten years have passed. Dirty or deep puncture wounds need a booster after five years, plus tetanus immunoglobulin if the person is unvaccinated.

rows: 3 or more doses; last 5 to 10 years

Give single Td booster + HTIG if high risk

steps.title: Surgical wound toilet and debridement
steps.tx: The foundation of wound management is meticulous **surgical wound debridement**, removing necrotic tissue, foreign dirt, soil and blood clots to restore oxygenated tissue perfusion that prevents anaerobic spore germination. Wounds are copiously irrigated with sterile saline, devitalised margins excised, puncture tracts widely unroofed, and primary suturing avoided in grossly contaminated crush injuries, accompanied by oral penicillin or metronidazole.
steps.say: Thorough surgical cleaning washes away dirt, removes dead tissue and restores oxygen to the wound. Flooding the tissues with oxygen prevents anaerobic tetanus spores from germinating.

nodes.label: Removal of embedded foreign dirt and soil
Open wound care to prevent anaerobic environment

steps.title: Management of clinical generalised tetanus
steps.tx: When clinical spasms develop, treatment requires immediate **intensive care management** in a darkened, quiet isolation room to minimize external sensory stimuli that trigger reflex spasms. Physicians administer intravenous human tetanus immunoglobulin, parenteral metronidazole to eliminate vegetative bacteria, intravenous diazepam infusions or magnesium sulphate to control muscle spasms, and early elective tracheostomy with neuromuscular blockade to prevent asphyxiation.
steps.say: Patients with established tetanus need intensive care in a quiet, darkened room. Treatment combines tetanus immunoglobulin, metronidazole, muscle relaxants and early tracheostomy.

rows: Destroys anaerobic bacteria at wound bed
IV diazepam infusions or magnesium sulphate
Calms reflex motor convulsions and rigidity
